how: Ariake Urban Sports Park, built for the Tokyo 2020 BMX racing and freestyle events, has reopened as a public leisure and sports park with skate and sports facilities; BMX-specific public sessions were not confirmed.
PADEL TOKYO mizumachi, opened by Tobu Railway in 2023 under the Skytree line in east Tokyo, offers padel courts for hire.
B-PUMP Tokyo Akihabara is one of Japan's largest climbing gyms with daily first-timer lessons; Tokyo also has many rope-climbing gyms, though top-rope at B-PUMP specifically was not confirmed.
Tokyo Glass Art in Ota Ward runs short walk-in glassblowing experiences where visitors blow their own piece.
Artbar Tokyo in Daikanyama runs painting sessions in English and Japanese, and International Art Studio in Minato offers painting and drawing classes in English.
Artbar Tokyo runs casual painting-and-drink sessions (watercolour sessions not specifically confirmed); Japanese-language art schools offer dedicated watercolour courses.

Wakasu Yacht Training School operates from a boathouse inside Wakasu Seaside Park on Tokyo Bay, run under the Tokyo metropolitan government; Sailability Tokyo also runs Hansa dinghy sessions at Toyosu.
Wakasu Yacht Training School in Wakasu Seaside Park teaches dinghy sailing on Tokyo Bay, and Hansa 303 dinghy sessions run from Toyosu.
Wakasu Seaside Park has a metropolitan-run camping ground on Tokyo Bay, and larger campsites operate in the Tama and Okutama areas.
Japan GAA, a volunteer-run club founded in 1995 with 300+ members, plays Gaelic football (and hurling) in Tokyo and welcomes new players.

Printmaking workshop Fuji Graphics in Taito offers one-off experiences choosing lithography, silkscreen or copperplate etching, and Machida City Museum of Graphic Arts runs a one-day etching (drypoint) course for beginners.
Printmaking workshop Fuji Graphics in Taito offers lithography experiences, and the Machida City Museum of Graphic Arts print studio runs lithography courses.
Printmaking workshop Fuji Graphics in Taito offers a 2-4 hour silkscreen experience for up to six people by reservation.
Beginner stained glass experiences run at several studios, such as Stainedglass Pastel in Taito, Atelier T&T in Setagaya and Stained House Amaud in Kunitachi.
Ardagh School of Irish Dance teaches in Tokyo, the first CLRG-accredited Irish dance school in Japan, taking children and adults from beginner to competitive level.
Rescue groups such as Buddies, ARK and Japan Cat Network place dogs and cats with adopters in Tokyo, with English-language processes for international residents.
Tokyo rescue groups such as ARK and Buddies accept volunteers and foster families, but a dedicated English-language shelter volunteer programme was not confirmed.
Zen temples and groups run English beginner zazen in and around Tokyo, including Dogen Sangha (Saturday sessions), Tokozenji and Sojiji in Yokohama, and Denchuji.

Shibuya has a cluster of public making spaces including FabLab Shibuya and FabCafe (part of Tokyo Fabbers) with 3D printers, laser cutters and electronics tools, and Tokyo Hackerspace-style groups meet regularly.
Candle Studio RADIUS in Chiyoda's Sanbancho runs candle-making classes, including Japanese-sweets aroma candles, by reservation.
TOKYO Whisky Library in Omotesando is a whisky lounge with over 1,000 bottles and a menu of tasting flights and staff who explain the selection.
Fine Vintage runs WSET Level 1 and 2 wine courses in Tokyo at the Westin Tokyo, and Academie du Vin Aoyama in Shibuya hosts WSET sake awards.
venue: Fine Vintage WSET at Westin Tokyo

how: The Japan Chess Federation (formerly National Chess Society of Japan) has a Chess Center in Ueno, Taito, and runs events such as the Tokyo Chess Festival; informal meetups also run at pubs.
Akihabara has e-sports Square and exeField Akiba gaming venues with banks of gaming PCs for play and tournaments, and Konami runs an esports arena in Ginza.
Hiko Mizuno College of Jewelry near Shibuya Station runs 2- and 3-year WOSTEP-affiliated watchmaking courses.
The Kite Museum Tokyo (Taimeiken) in Nihonbashi holds 100+ kites with kite-making demonstrations and classes, and Wakasu Seaside Park and riverbank parks have open areas for flying.

The Tokyo Orienteering Association and the Tama Orienteering Club organise park and urban orienteering events in the Tokyo area, such as the All Japan Trail Orienteering Championships at Nogawa Park, plus student-run Tokyo Orienteering events.

No indoor snow slope operates in central Tokyo (the Funabashi ski dome closed), but Sayama Ski Resort in Saitama has a 300 m indoor slope about 40-60 minutes by train and Snova Shin-Yokohama has a 60 m slope.
The Philatelic Museum (Kitte no Hakubutsukan) in Mejiro holds around 350,000 stamps, with a specialist library and changing exhibitions.

The Japan Cricket Association is headquartered in Minato and runs leagues with Tokyo clubs (Tokyo Wombats, Tokyo Titans, university teams), with Akishima a designated cricket city, but the main international ground at Sano is 80-90 km away.
Shibuya street dance studios such as En Dance Studio hold regular classes, and Tokyo's breaking scene is described as one of the world's biggest, with Shibuya battles.
The National Museum of Nature and Science in Ueno has Earth-history galleries and hands-on programmes for viewing fossils and specimens; field collecting sites are outside Tokyo.
venue: National Museum of Nature and Science
